rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Inclusive business accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Treat it as inclusive because serving an underserved need is the primary purpose and the model always sustains itself.

key.explanation: An inclusive business must always do both: meet a specific need of underserved people, and remain financially sustainable.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Replicating rural services accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Use a controlled partner model with local credibility and standards every partner must meet.

key.explanation: Rural service models scale through trusted local partners rather than capital-heavy control, under standards every partner must meet.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Rural BPO model accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Choose suitable domestic processes, train local staff, and adapt operations without relaxing client service standards.

key.explanation: RuralShores adapted BPO work, training and location to rural conditions while never relaxing the service quality clients buy on.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Impact investing accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Classify it as impact investing because intent, measurement and return are all designed together.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Intent defines the desired change, measurement tests whether it occurred, and return keeps investment capital reusable.

key.explanation: Impact investing needs all three of intent, measurement and financial return present together; it is never a grant.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains Social business accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Judge whether the social goal drives the model and discipline keeps it running, never letting profit become the purpose.

key.explanation: A social business puts social impact first inside a no-loss operating model, and never depends only on periodic donations.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Group-based microfinance accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Use formed groups, staged lending and local monitoring, which works only while repayment capacity stays real.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Local information can reduce screening risk, but the structure works only when repayment capacity and group discipline remain real.

key.explanation: The classic Grameen model lent without collateral using group knowledge and peer accountability, which holds only while repayment capacity stays real.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Responsible lending accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Pause lending, assess total obligations and cash flow, and never let volume incentives outrun borrower capacity.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Access becomes harmful when debt service outruns income; scale must preserve the screening practices that made inclusion viable.

key.explanation: Responsible lending checks total debt and repayment capacity, and never lets loan volume outrun the screening that made inclusion viable.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Applies Farmer Producer Organisation accurately to this case; the exact term need not be named if the idea is clearly used.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Aggregate through a farmer-owned organisation and build market links, because scale never becomes income without them.

rubric.label: Case evidence and reasoning
rubric.description: Uses a specific fact from the case and explains why it supports the decision: Collective ownership turns fragmented production into scale, but market access and managerial capability convert that scale into income.

key.explanation: An FPO pools farmer ownership and volume, but that scale never becomes income without market access and managerial capability.

rubric.label: Course understanding
rubric.description: Explains SELCO affordability system accurately in the learner's own words; the exact term is optional when the idea is clear.

rubric.label: Decision use
rubric.description: Explains when the idea should change a decision, consistently with this course move: Bundle the light with finance and dependable service, since removing any one of those links makes it unusable.

key.explanation: SELCO linked solar products, independent finance and reliable service into one system, where removing any single link makes the offer unusable.
